_how: Your words per sub-claim (MKT-01-A ...). Leave proposed_action empty to let the rules decide. review_status: DRAFT / READY FOR REVIEW / APPROVED / HOLD / RETURN. cross_refs: ids in other members' files, e.g. EDU-E001.

MKT-01-A.conclusion: Partly supported. Singapore teachers spend 6.4 h/week marking (OECD TALIS 2024, MKT-E020) and differentiated primary teaching doubles preparation time (MKT-E017); initial diagnostic assessment adds to primary teachers' workload (MKT-E024), and studies elsewhere show diagnosing maths misconceptions is demanding (MKT-E022, MKT-E023). No evidence specific to tutors or tuition centres.
MKT-01-A.action_reason: Set by Hansle 2026-11-04: teacher time on assessment is supported (TALIS 2024, diagnosis studies); limits stated.

MKT-01-B.conclusion: Partly supported. Automated grading cut teacher grading time by 35% (MKT-E028) and teachers value adaptive diagnostic assessment (MKT-E025); Singapore households spent S$1.8b on tuition in 2023 (MKT-E002). No public evidence that tuition centres pay for diagnostic software.

MKT-01-C.conclusion: Weakly supported. Teachers adopt learning-analytics tools when they expect better performance (MKT-E032) and use dashboards to find struggling students (MKT-E029), but all evidence is from schools or universities. Needs primary research with Singapore tuition centres.

MKT-01-D.conclusion: Not established. MOE publishes student counts (237,966 primary students in 2024, MKT-E006) but no count of tuition centres, and MOE does not track the industry's size. Market size must remain an explicit assumption.

MKT-02-A.conclusion: Largely contradicted on diagnosis: Geniebook, KooBits and MOE SLS already identify learning gaps and report them (MKT-E004, MKT-E009, MKT-E019, MKT-E010). Not found in public material: tutor-reviewed, evidence-traceable reports licensed to tuition centres.
MKT-02-A.action_reason: Set by Hansle 2026-11-04: reviewed counter-evidence shows competitors already identify and report learning gaps.

MKT-02-B.conclusion: Synthetic by design: MathBridge's features are fictional (SYN-02). Against the Competitor Matrix, its distinguishing features are tutor review, response-level evidence links and a centre licence.

MKT-02-C.conclusion: Indirectly supported. Expert human feedback is more nuanced than AI alone (MKT-E036) and explained diagnostic results help teachers plan better (MKT-E039). No evidence that tuition centres value or would pay for these features.
